title: Creating NuGet Packages
description: How to pack and publish your own libraries as NuGet packages.

data.text: Any class library can become a NuGet package: add package metadata to the `.csproj`, run `dotnet pack`, and a `.nupkg` file appears in `bin/Release`. The package id must be unique on the target feed and the version must increase with every publish.

data.title: Create and configure a library
data.content: Start from the classlib template, then add the metadata NuGet needs.
data.code:
dotnet new classlib -n MyAwesomeLib
dotnet new gitignore

data.title: Project metadata for packing
data.content: These properties are written into the generated .nuspec. `IsPackable` is true for class libraries by default.
data.code:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <PackageId>MyAwesomeLib</PackageId>
    <Version>1.2.0</Version>
    <Authors>YourName</Authors>
    <Company>Contoso</Company>
    <Description>A brief description shown in the feed and IDE.</Description>
    <PackageTags>utility;json</PackageTags>
    <PackageLicenseExpression>MIT</PackageLicenseExpression>
    <RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/contoso/MyAwesomeLib</RepositoryUrl>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>

data.title: Pack and publish
data.content: `dotnet pack` builds and produces the .nupkg; `dotnet nuget push` uploads it. Use `--skip-duplicate` so re-running CI does not fail on an existing version.
data.code:
dotnet pack -c Release

# Publish to nuget.org (key comes from a secret store, never source control)
dotnet nuget push bin/Release/MyAwesomeLib.1.2.0.nupkg \
  --api-key $NUGET_API_KEY \
  --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json \
  --skip-duplicate

# Or publish to a private feed
# dotnet nuget push bin/Release/MyAwesomeLib.1.2.0.nupkg --source MyPrivateFeed

data.title: Versioning rules
data.text: Semantic versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) communicates intent: PATCH for compatible fixes, MINOR for compatible additions, MAJOR for breaking changes. NuGet treats `1.0.0` and `1.0.0.0` as equal, and a package version on a feed is immutable — you cannot overwrite it, only publish a new one.

data.title: Common mistakes
items: Publishing a version that already exists on the feed (fails permanently; bump the version instead).
Forgetting `<GenerateDocumentationFile>` so consumers get no IntelliSense descriptions.
Reusing a personal API key in a build script or committing it — use a scoped key or CI secret.
Packing the test project by accident; set `<IsPackable>false</IsPackable>` in test projects.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `PackageId`, `Version`, and `Authors` are the minimum metadata for a package
`dotnet pack` produces the .nupkg; `dotnet nuget push` publishes it
Keep API keys out of source control and pass them as CI secrets
Version numbers are immutable once published
data.takeaway: Packing a library correctly makes it reusable across projects and easy for others to consume.
